sec: Anterior delt, triceps, serratus anterior, anterior core
tech: Hands just outside shoulder width, elbows tracking about 45 degrees from the torso, body in one line from head to heels, chest to within a fist of the floor, full lockout with the shoulder blades allowed to protract.
mist: Elbows flared to 90 degrees, which loads the shoulder capsule. Hips sagging or piking, which turns it into a partial rep. Cutting depth once fatigue arrives.
prog: Add vest load, elevate the feet, slow the eccentric, or move to archer.
reg: Elevate the hands on a surface until you can hold a rigid line.
use: Main pressing volume on push work, or a high-rep back-off set after dips.
mob: Doorway pec stretch, Thoracic extension over a rolled towel

tech: Hands on a counter, bench, or the dip bars, same rigid line and same elbow path as a floor push-up. The higher the hands, the easier the rep.
mist: Letting the hips lead so the torso bends. Choosing a surface so high the set stops being challenging.
prog: Lower the surface a step at a time until you are on the floor.
reg: Raise the surface, or press into a wall.
use: Regression, warm-up ramp, or high-rep finisher when fatigued.

tech: Feet on a surface roughly 12 to 24 inches high, hands on the floor. The higher the feet, the more the load shifts toward the clavicular fibres and the front delt.
mist: Letting the hips pike to dodge the load. Going so high that it becomes a pike push-up and stops being a chest movement.
prog: Raise the feet, add a vest, or add a deficit under the hands.
reg: Lower the feet to the floor.
use: Best home substitute for incline pressing. Run it early on upper days.
mob: Doorway pec stretch at a high hand position

tech: Standard push-up mechanics with the vest sitting high on the trunk so the load stays over the chest rather than dragging the hips down.
mist: Loading the vest so heavily that the rep speed collapses. Letting the added mass pull the lumbar spine into extension.
prog: Add vest weight in small jumps, then elevate the feet with the vest on.
reg: Strip vest weight or elevate the hands.
use: The cleanest way to keep push-ups in a hypertrophy rep range once bodyweight sets exceed 20 reps.

tech: Hands on parallettes or dumbbell handles so the chest can travel below the hands. Control the extra range and pause briefly at the bottom.
mist: Bouncing out of the deep position. Allowing the shoulders to shrug up toward the ears at the bottom.
prog: Add vest load or elevate the feet.
reg: Reduce the height of the handles or return to floor push-ups.
use: Excellent stretch-biased chest work. Lengthened-position loading is one of the more reliable hypertrophy levers.
mob: Doorway pec stretch, Shoulder extension stretch

tech: Four to five seconds down, brief pause an inch off the floor, normal speed up.
mist: Rushing the last third of the descent. Using the tempo as an excuse to shorten the range.
prog: Add vest load or lengthen the eccentric to six seconds.
use: Useful when equipment is limited and you need more stimulus from the same load.

tech: Wide hand placement, lower toward one hand while the opposite arm straightens and acts as a light outrigger. Keep the hips square.
mist: Rotating the hips to shorten the range. Pushing hard through the straight arm so it stops being unilateral.
prog: Reduce assistance from the straight arm, then move toward one-arm work.
reg: Narrow the stance of the hands or use a band under the straight arm.
use: Strength bridge toward one-arm pressing and a good symmetry tool for your left-side deficit.
mob: Doorway pec stretch, Wrist mobility flow

sec: Anterior delt, biceps tendon, serratus, core
tech: Hands at hip level, shoulders leaning well forward of the hands, scapulae protracted, body leaning through the whole rep.
mist: Losing the forward lean as the set fatigues. Letting the lower back arch instead of holding a posterior pelvic tilt.
prog: Increase the forward lean, elevate the feet, or move to tuck planche work.
reg: Reduce the lean or elevate the hands.
use: Doubles as planche-specific strength work on skill days.
mob: Wrist mobility flow, Anterior shoulder stretch

tech: Feet wide, working hand under the shoulder, free hand behind the back. Start elevated and lower the surface over months, not weeks.
mist: Twisting the torso so the shoulder rather than the chest takes the load. Progressing the height faster than technique holds.
prog: Lower the surface height, then reduce foot spread.
reg: Raise the surface or return to archer push-ups.
use: A strength skill rather than an efficient hypertrophy driver. Train it fresh, not at the end of a session.

tech: Fast eccentric, aggressive concentric so the hands leave the floor, soft landing with the elbows absorbing.
mist: Grinding out reps to fatigue, which defeats the point. Landing with locked elbows.
prog: Add a clap, then a vest at low load.
reg: Push hard enough to unload the hands without leaving the floor.
use: Early in a push session for rate of force development. Keep total reps low.

tech: Rings set low, turn the rings out at lockout, allow a slight fly path at the bottom for extra chest stretch.
mist: Letting the rings drift apart under fatigue. Turning it into a fly and losing the press.
prog: Lower the ring height, elevate the feet, add a vest.
reg: Raise the rings toward chest height.
use: High stability demand, so use it for chest volume rather than top-end strength. Requires a hang point.
mob: Doorway pec stretch, Shoulder controlled circles

tech: Lean the torso forward roughly 30 degrees, elbows drift slightly wide, descend until the upper arm is a little past parallel, press back without fully locking if the elbows complain.
mist: Dropping below a comfortable shoulder position in search of range. Losing the forward lean, which shifts the work to triceps.
prog: Add vest load, then pause at the bottom.
reg: Use a band for assistance or perform slow negatives from the top.
use: One of the two best chest builders available to you. Run it as a primary press.
mob: Doorway pec stretch, Shoulder extension stretch

tech: Same mechanics as the bodyweight dip with the vest on. Control the descent, no bouncing at the bottom.
mist: Adding load before the bodyweight version is smooth for 12 clean reps. Shortening range as load climbs.
prog: Add vest weight in small increments and rebuild the rep range.
use: Your closest available equivalent to a heavy compound press. Treat it like a main lift.
mob: Doorway pec stretch, Anterior shoulder stretch

tech: Support hold with rings turned out, descend under control, keep the rings close to the ribs, press and re-turn the rings at the top.
mist: Letting the rings swing wide. Attempting these before bar dips are comfortable for 12 reps.
prog: Add a vest, add a bottom pause, or progress toward ring muscle-ups.
reg: Return to bar dips or use a foot-assisted setup.
use: Skill and stability work. Requires a hang point.
mob: Shoulder controlled circles, Doorway pec stretch

tech: Lie on the floor, knees bent, elbows about 45 degrees, lower until the triceps touch the floor, brief pause, press without clashing the dumbbells.
mist: Bouncing the elbows off the floor. Pressing the dumbbells together at the top and losing tension.
prog: Increase load or add a two-second bottom pause.
reg: Reduce load and slow the eccentric.
use: The floor limits range, which is actually kinder on the shoulder. Good heavy pressing option without a bench.

tech: Press two dumbbells together hard throughout the set and press from the chest to lockout while maintaining the inward squeeze.
mist: Relaxing the squeeze during the descent. Using dumbbells too heavy to keep them pinned together.
prog: Add load or add a squeeze hold at lockout.
use: One of the few ways to load adduction without cables. Good finisher after dips or floor press.

tech: Slight elbow bend held constant, arms open until the upper arms touch the floor, then arc back up thinking about pulling the elbows toward each other.
mist: Turning it into a press by bending the elbows. Loading heavy enough that the shoulder takes over at the bottom.
prog: Add load slowly, or pause two seconds at the stretched position.
reg: Reduce load or increase elbow bend.
use: Accessory only. The floor caps the stretch, so treat it as adduction volume rather than a stretch movement.

tech: Lie across or along a stable surface, one dumbbell held with both hands, arms nearly straight, lower behind the head until you feel a deep stretch through the ribs and lats, pull back over the chest.
mist: Letting the ribs flare and the lower back arch. Bending the elbows and turning it into a triceps extension.
prog: Add load or increase the pause in the stretched position.
use: One of the better lengthened-position lat movements you can do without cables.
mob: Lat stretch on a doorframe, Thoracic extension over a rolled towel

tech: Set a stable surface to roughly 30 degrees, feet planted, lower the dumbbells to the upper chest with elbows at about 45 degrees, press without clashing.
mist: Using an unstable improvised incline. Setting the angle too steep so it becomes a shoulder press.
prog: Increase load or add a bottom pause.
reg: Reduce load or use feet-elevated push-ups instead.
use: Optional. Only run this if you have a genuinely stable incline. Otherwise feet-elevated push-ups cover the same job.
mob: Doorway pec stretch at a high hand position

tech: Anchor the band behind you at chest height, step forward into tension, sweep the hands together and hold the squeeze for a beat.
mist: Using so much tension that the torso rotates. Letting the shoulders roll forward at the finish.
prog: Shorten the band or step further from the anchor.
reg: Lengthen the band or reduce range.
use: Pump work and pre-activation. Band tension peaks where the chest is strongest, which is the opposite of ideal, so keep it accessory.

sec: Teres major, lower and middle traps, rhomboids, biceps, forearms
tech: Pronated grip just outside shoulder width, start from a full hang with the shoulder blades allowed to elevate, pull the elbows down and back until the chin clears, control the descent to a full hang.
mist: Kipping or bouncing out of the bottom. Stopping short of a full hang, which removes the most productive part of the range. Leading with the chin instead of the chest.
prog: Add vest load, pause at the top, or slow the eccentric.
reg: Band assistance or negatives from the top.
use: The single highest-value movement you own. Anchor every pull session with it.
mob: Lat stretch on a doorframe, Dead hang decompression

tech: Supinated grip at shoulder width, full hang to chest touching the bar, elbows drive down and slightly forward.
mist: Allowing the elbows to drift forward at the bottom and losing lat tension. Cutting the bottom range because the biceps fatigue first.
prog: Add vest load or slow the eccentric.
use: Slightly more biceps than a pull-up and usually the stronger of the two. Good for loaded progression.
mob: Biceps and forearm stretch against a wall, Dead hang decompression

sec: Teres major, traps, rhomboids, biceps, grip
tech: Vest on, same full-range mechanics. Do not sacrifice depth for load.
mist: Adding weight before 10 clean bodyweight reps. Half reps once the added load gets heavy.
prog: Add vest weight in small jumps, then rebuild reps to the top of the range.
use: Your primary heavy pull. This is the lift most responsible for back and lat thickness given your equipment.
mob: Lat stretch on a doorframe, Dead hang decompression

tech: Palms facing each other on parallel handles or rings, pull the chest toward the hands, full hang between reps.
mist: Shrugging at the top instead of depressing the shoulder blades. Short range at the bottom.
prog: Add vest load or pause at the top.
use: Usually the most shoulder-friendly grip. Good default when the elbows or shoulders are irritated.

tech: Grip roughly one and a half shoulder widths, pull the chest to the bar with the elbows driving down and out.
mist: Grip so wide the range collapses to a few inches. Shrugging the shoulders up through the pull.
prog: Add vest load or pause at the top.
reg: Narrow the grip toward shoulder width.
use: Slightly more width emphasis than a standard pull-up. Range matters more than grip width, so do not go extreme.

tech: Wide grip, pull toward one hand while the opposite arm stays nearly straight along the bar.
mist: Letting the straight arm pull hard, which removes the point. Twisting the torso to reduce the range.
prog: Reduce the assistance from the straight arm, then move toward one-arm negatives.
reg: Narrow the grip or use a band.
use: Bridge toward one-arm pulling and a direct answer to your left-side deficit.
mob: Lat stretch on a doorframe, Thoracic rotation

tech: Hold the legs at or above hip height throughout, pull without letting the legs drop or swing.
mist: Legs dropping progressively through the set. Using a leg swing to start each rep.
prog: Raise the leg height or add ankle load.
reg: Use a tuck position instead of a full L.
use: Combines heavy pulling with hard anterior core compression. Low volume, high quality.
mob: Hamstring floor stretch, Dead hang decompression

tech: Jump or step to the top position, then lower over five to eight seconds to a full hang.
mist: Dropping through the last third of the descent. Letting the shoulders disconnect at the bottom.
prog: Lengthen the descent or add vest load.
reg: Shorten the descent to three seconds.
use: The fastest route from few pull-ups to many, and a useful overload tool even when strong.

tech: Loop the band over the bar and place a knee or foot in it. Assistance is greatest at the bottom, which is where most people fail.
mist: Using a band so thick the movement becomes a bounce. Never reducing band thickness.
prog: Move to a thinner band, then to unassisted work.
use: Volume tool for extra pull-up sets after unassisted work is done.

tech: Hang with straight arms, depress and retract the shoulder blades to raise the body an inch or two without bending the elbows, then release back to a full hang.
mist: Bending the elbows and turning it into a partial pull-up. Rushing the reps.
prog: Add a two-second hold at the top or add vest load.
reg: Perform with the feet lightly supported.
use: Warm-up before every pull session and a genuine fix for the shoulder position you need for planche and pull-up strength.
mob: Dead hang decompression, Shoulder controlled circles

tech: Full passive hang, relaxed shoulders, breathe. Progress total accumulated time.
mist: Gripping so hard the forearms fail before the hang does its job. Holding the breath.
prog: Add time, then add vest load, then move to one-arm hangs.
reg: Keep the feet lightly on the floor.
use: Grip work, shoulder decompression, and a quarter to half inch of temporary height recovery. Cheap and worth doing daily.

tech: Build from explosive chest-to-bar pull-ups and straight-bar dips, then practise the transition with a false grip and a fast turnover.
mist: Chasing the skill before owning 10 strict pull-ups and 12 clean dips. Training it fatigued, which teaches a sloppy transition.
prog: Progress from high pull-ups to slow negatives to strict reps.
reg: Return to chest-to-bar pull-ups and straight-bar dips.
use: Skill work. Train it fresh on a skill day, not for hypertrophy.
mob: Wrist mobility flow, Shoulder controlled circles

eq: Pull-up bar; Rings (needs hang point); Elevated surface
tech: Set the bar at hip height, body straight, pull the sternum to the bar with the elbows at about 45 degrees, squeeze the blades together at the top.
mist: Hips sagging so the row becomes a partial. Yanking with the arms without retracting the scapulae.
prog: Elevate the feet, add a vest, or pause at the top.
reg: Raise the bar or bend the knees.
use: The horizontal pull your program needs. Upper back thickness and posture both live here.
mob: Thoracic extension over a rolled towel, Pec minor release

eq: Pull-up bar; Elevated surface; Weighted vest
tech: Feet on a box or chair so the torso is level or slightly head-down, same pull to the sternum.
mist: Letting the hips drop when the set gets hard. Shrugging instead of retracting.
prog: Add a vest, add a top pause, or lower the bar.
reg: Return the feet to the floor.
use: The heaviest horizontal pull you can load without a barbell.
mob: Thoracic extension over a rolled towel

tech: Rings at hip height, body rigid, pull with the rings turning out at the top so the palms finish facing forward.
mist: Letting the rings drift wide. Losing the plank line at the hips.
prog: Elevate the feet or add a vest.
reg: Walk the feet back to a more upright angle.
use: Rotation at the top adds external rotation work that most rowing misses. Requires a hang point.
mob: Pec minor release, Shoulder controlled circles

sec: Mid traps, rear delt, biceps, obliques
tech: Support the free hand on a stable surface, hips square, torso near horizontal, pull the dumbbell toward the hip with the elbow tracking close to the ribs, full stretch at the bottom without letting the shoulder collapse forward.
mist: Rotating the torso to heave the weight up. Cutting the stretch at the bottom. Pulling to the armpit rather than the hip when the goal is lats.
prog: Add load, add a one-second squeeze, or slow the eccentric.
reg: Reduce load and shorten the lever by supporting more weight on the free arm.
use: Your best unilateral back builder and the direct fix for the six percent arm asymmetry in your scan.
mob: Lat stretch on a doorframe, Thoracic rotation

tech: Chest on an inclined stable surface, arms hanging, row with the elbows at about 45 degrees and pause briefly at the top.
mist: Peeling the chest off the support to cheat the last reps. Using momentum from the legs.
prog: Add load or lengthen the top pause.
use: Removes lower back and hip involvement, so it is the cleanest way to add back volume when systemically fatigued.
mob: Thoracic extension over a rolled towel

tech: Hinge to roughly 15 degrees above horizontal, neutral spine, row both dumbbells to the lower ribs, control the descent.
mist: Standing more upright as the set fatigues. Rounding the lower back under load.
prog: Add load or reduce the torso angle toward horizontal.
reg: Use the one-arm supported version instead.
use: Efficient bilateral back volume, but it taxes the erectors, so place it away from hinge work.

tech: Lie face down on a raised stable surface, arms hanging straight down, row with strict scapular retraction and no torso movement.
mist: Using body english that the position is designed to eliminate. Loading too heavy for the strict position.
prog: Add load or pause two seconds at the top.
use: Strictest upper back option you have. Excellent for rear delt and rhomboid detail.

tech: Hinged or chest-supported, row with the elbows flared to about 90 degrees, pulling toward the upper ribs and armpits.
mist: Confusing this with a lat row and pulling to the hip. Shrugging into the traps.
prog: Add load or add a top pause.
use: Rear delt and upper back thickness. Pairs well with lat-biased pulling in the same session.
mob: Pec minor release, Thoracic extension over a rolled towel

tech: Heavy dumbbells at the sides, shrug straight up toward the ears, pause one second at the top, lower under control through a full range.
mist: Rolling the shoulders, which adds nothing and irritates the joint. Bouncing with the knees.
prog: Add load or lengthen the top hold.
use: Traps read as thickness from the front and support neck and shoulder framing. Straps help once your grip limits you.

tech: Face down, very light dumbbells, arms raised overhead in a Y with the thumbs up, driven by the shoulder blades sliding down and back.
mist: Using weight heavy enough to recruit the upper traps. Arching the lower back to lift the arms higher.
prog: Add a two-second hold at the top before adding load.
use: Direct lower trap work, which supports overhead position and counters the desk and phone posture pattern.
mob: Thoracic extension over a rolled towel

sec: Long head of triceps, teres major
tech: Band anchored overhead, slight elbow bend held constant, pull the hands down to the thighs by driving the humerus down, squeeze the lats, control back up.
mist: Bending the elbows and turning it into a triceps pushdown. Leaning forward to add leverage.
prog: Shorten the band or add a squeeze at the bottom.
use: The only isolated lat movement available without cables. Excellent pull-day warm-up and finisher.

tech: Anchor the band overhead, kneel, pull the hands to the collarbone with the elbows driving down, hold one second at the bottom.
mist: Leaning back so far it becomes a row. Letting the band snap the arms up.
prog: Shorten the band or double it.
reg: Lengthen the band or step closer.
use: Warm-up, pump work, or a low-fatigue lat option on red-light days.

tech: Hold a tuck front lever with the hips level, pull the body toward the bar keeping the torso horizontal, lower under control.
mist: Letting the hips drop below the shoulders. Losing the posterior pelvic tilt.
prog: Move from tuck to advanced tuck to straddle.
reg: Hold the static position only, or use a deeper tuck.
use: Straight-arm lat strength that carries directly into planche and front lever work.
mob: Lat stretch on a doorframe, Dead hang decompression

tech: Anchor the feet, hips on a padded edge, lower until the torso hangs, extend back to a straight line without hyperextending.
mist: Cranking into hyperextension at the top. Rushing the reps.
prog: Hold a dumbbell at the chest or pause at the top.
reg: Reduce range or use a floor superman instead.
use: Erector work supports posture and hinge strength, both of which read visually and protect you during long electrical work days.

tech: Face down, lift the chest, arms, and legs a few inches, reach long rather than high, keep the neck neutral.
mist: Cranking the neck up to look forward. Lifting high rather than reaching long.
prog: Add time, hold light dumbbells, or move to back extensions.
use: Low-cost posterior chain isometric for warm-ups or recovery days.

tech: Slight forward lean, small elbow bend held constant, raise to just above shoulder height leading with the elbow, lower under control over two to three seconds.
mist: Swinging the torso to start each rep. Going too heavy so the traps take over. Cutting the eccentric short.
prog: Add load, add a lengthened partial after failure, or slow the eccentric to four seconds.
reg: Reduce load or perform seated against a wall.
use: Non-negotiable for you. Side delts are your most direct route to visual width and one of your named lagging areas. Four to six sets per week minimum, ideally more.
mob: Shoulder controlled circles, Upper trap and levator stretch

tech: Hold a doorframe or upright with one hand and lean away, raise the free-side dumbbell. Leaning increases tension at the bottom of the range.
mist: Pulling with the anchoring arm to help the raise. Letting the torso swing.
prog: Add load or increase the lean angle.
use: The closest thing you have to a cable lateral raise. Excellent second lateral movement in the same session.

tech: Standing or seated, dumbbells at shoulder height with the forearms vertical, press up and slightly in without letting the ribs flare, lower to ear level.
mist: Arching the lower back to press heavier. Stopping the descent well above the ears.
prog: Add load, pause at the bottom, or move to a seated version to remove leg drive.
reg: Reduce load or perform seated with back support.
use: Your primary vertical press. Standing costs some load but adds real core demand.
mob: Thoracic extension over a rolled towel, Wall slide

tech: Seated upright with the back supported, press without leg drive, full range from ears to lockout.
mist: Letting the elbows drift far forward. Bouncing out of the bottom.
prog: Add load or add a bottom pause.
use: More strict than standing, so slightly better for pure delt hypertrophy.

tech: Start with the palms facing you at chest height, rotate out as you press, reverse on the way down.
mist: Rotating after the press rather than during it. Loading heavy enough that the rotation is skipped.
prog: Add load or slow the rotation.
use: Adds a little extra range through the front delt. Accessory, not a main press.

tech: Hips high, torso close to vertical, lower the crown of the head toward the floor between the hands, press back up.
mist: Letting the hips drop so it becomes a decline push-up. Flaring the elbows straight out.
prog: Elevate the feet to increase the vertical angle, then add a deficit with parallettes.
use: Vertical pressing that costs nothing and builds toward handstand push-ups.

tech: Feet on a box, torso near vertical, head lowers to the floor between the hands.
mist: Cutting depth as the set fatigues. Letting the lower back arch.
prog: Add a deficit with parallettes, then progress toward wall handstand push-ups.
reg: Return the feet to the floor.
use: Heaviest bodyweight vertical press before handstand work.
mob: Wrist mobility flow, Thoracic extension over a rolled towel

tech: Kick up facing the wall or back to the wall, body stacked, lower the head to the floor under control, press to full lockout.
mist: Piking at the hips to make the press easier. Crashing the head into the floor.
prog: Add a deficit with parallettes, then reduce wall assistance.
use: Skill plus heavy vertical press. Train it fresh on skill days.
mob: Wrist mobility flow, Shoulder controlled circles

tech: Hinged at the hips or chest supported, small constant elbow bend, sweep the arms out and slightly back, pause at the top.
mist: Rowing instead of flying. Using momentum from the torso.
prog: Add load or add a top hold.
reg: Reduce load or use the prone version.
use: Rear delts are almost always undertrained and directly affect how three-dimensional the shoulder looks. Two to four sets weekly minimum.

tech: Face down on an elevated stable surface, arms hanging, raise out to the sides with the thumbs slightly up.
mist: Letting the chest rise off the surface. Going heavy and shrugging.
prog: Add load or hold at the top for two seconds.
use: Strictest rear delt option. Ideal when you want quality over load.

tech: Band anchored at face height, pull toward the forehead while rotating the hands back so the knuckles finish beside the ears.
mist: Turning it into a high row with no rotation. Using tension so high the elbows drop.
prog: Shorten the band or hold two seconds at the end range.
use: Best single movement for shoulder health and the rounded-forward posture your desk and phone time creates. Two to four sets weekly, done anywhere.

tech: Wide hand spacing, pull the elbows out and up to about shoulder height, no higher.
mist: Pulling above shoulder height, which pinches the shoulder for many people. Narrow spacing that loads the biceps.
prog: Add load or pause at the top.
reg: Reduce range or switch to lateral raises.
use: Optional. If it causes any shoulder pinch, drop it and run lateral raises instead. No unique benefit.

tech: Raise to eye level with a neutral or pronated grip, control the descent.
mist: Swinging from the hips. Adding volume when pressing already covers the front delt.
prog: Add load or slow the eccentric.
use: Lowest priority delt movement. Your pressing already hammers the front delt. Include only if the front delt is visually lagging, which it is not.

tech: Very light dumbbells, elbows at 90 degrees and raised to shoulder height, rotate the forearms up to vertical, then reverse.
mist: Using anything heavier than five to ten pounds. Letting the elbows drop during rotation.
prog: Add a hold at the top rather than load.
use: Prehab. Rotator cuff strength keeps heavy dips and presses available long term.
mob: Shoulder controlled circles, Pec minor release

tech: Stack wrists, shoulders and hips, ribs down, push the floor away, hold. Wall-supported first, then freestanding attempts.
mist: Banana back from ribs flaring. Practising to failure, which teaches poor position.
prog: Reduce wall contact, then work toward freestanding balance.
reg: Use a pike hold against a wall or an elevated pike.
use: Skill work that builds shoulder stability and directly supports planche progression.
mob: Wrist mobility flow, Shoulder controlled circles

tech: Hands on parallettes, shoulders leaning well forward of the hands, scapulae protracted and depressed, knees tucked, feet off the floor.
mist: Letting the shoulders sit behind the hands, which removes the lean. Rushing to advanced tuck before the basic hold is solid for 20 seconds.
prog: Move toward advanced tuck, then straddle, extending the hips a little at a time.
reg: Use a frog stand or elevate the hands higher.
use: Your stated skill goal. Train it fresh at the start of skill days with long rests and total accumulated time as the metric.
mob: Wrist mobility flow, Biceps and forearm stretch against a wall

tech: Pike push-up mechanics with the vest on. Keep the vest tight so it does not slide toward the head.
mist: Loading before clean feet-elevated pike push-ups exist. Letting the vest change the hip position.
prog: Add vest weight, then elevate the feet.
use: Loads vertical pressing progressively without a barbell.

tech: Seated on the floor with the legs straight, press overhead without leaning back. The floor removes every cheat available.
mist: Rounding the lower back to gain leverage. Loading anywhere near your standing press weight.
prog: Add load slowly or pause at the top.
reg: Sit against a wall or bend the knees.
use: Brutal core and thoracic position check. Exposes and fixes the rib flare that shows up in overhead pressing.
mob: Standing hamstring hinge stretch, Thoracic extension over a rolled towel

tech: Raise the dumbbells in the scapular plane, roughly 30 degrees forward of straight out to the sides, thumbs up.
mist: Drifting into a front raise. Shrugging at the top.
prog: Add load or slow the eccentric.
use: Often more comfortable than a strict lateral raise for irritated shoulders, with almost the same effect.

tech: Arms straight at chest height, pull the band apart until it touches the sternum, squeeze, return slowly.
mist: Bending the elbows. Shrugging the shoulders up.
prog: Shorten the band or add a hold at end range.
use: Warm-up staple before any pressing, and free posture volume on rest days.

tech: Elbows pinned at the sides, curl with supination, squeeze at the top, lower over two to three seconds to full extension.
mist: Swinging the torso to start the rep. Stopping short of full elbow extension. Letting the elbows drift forward.
prog: Add load, slow the eccentric, or add a lengthened partial after failure.
use: Direct biceps volume. Aaliyah named biceps as a priority, and they respond fast at your training age.
mob: Biceps and forearm stretch against a wall

tech: Recline on a surface at roughly 45 to 60 degrees, arms hanging behind the torso, curl without letting the shoulder flex forward.
mist: Letting the elbows swing forward to shorten the range. Sitting too upright and losing the stretch.
prog: Add load or pause two seconds at the stretched position.
use: Best long-head builder you have. Stretch-position loading is where the biceps respond most.
mob: Biceps and forearm stretch against a wall

tech: Neutral grip throughout, elbows at the sides, curl to the shoulder, control the descent.
mist: Swinging. Rotating into a supinated curl at the top.
prog: Add load or slow the eccentric.
use: Brachialis growth pushes the biceps up and adds arm width from the front. Pairs with supinated curls, not a replacement.
mob: Biceps and forearm stretch against a wall

tech: Curl the dumbbell across the body toward the opposite shoulder, keeping the upper arm still.
mist: Rotating the torso. Letting the elbow travel across the body.
prog: Add load or add a squeeze at the top.
use: Slight brachialis emphasis and often more comfortable on the wrist than a straight hammer curl.
mob: Biceps and forearm stretch against a wall

tech: Seated, elbow braced against the inner thigh, curl with full supination and a hard peak contraction.
mist: Using the leg to help. Rushing the eccentric.
prog: Add load or hold the peak for two seconds.
use: Strictest curl variation. Good for chasing the left-right balance in your scan.
mob: Biceps and forearm stretch against a wall

tech: Shoulder-width supinated grip, think about driving the elbows down and bringing the forearm to the upper arm rather than the chest to the bar.
mist: Hollow-body swinging. Cutting the bottom range.
prog: Add vest load.
use: The only loadable compound biceps movement you own. Heavier than any curl you can do.
mob: Biceps and forearm stretch against a wall

tech: Lean back under a low bar or rings holding a supinated grip, elbows high and fixed, curl the body up toward the hands.
mist: Letting the elbows drop and turning it into a row. Losing the straight body line.
prog: Walk the feet further forward or elevate them.
use: Loads the biceps with body mass. Useful when dumbbells feel light for high-rep sets.
mob: Biceps and forearm stretch against a wall

tech: Curl up supinated, rotate to pronated at the top, lower slowly in the pronated position, rotate back at the bottom.
mist: Rushing the pronated eccentric, which is the whole point. Going too heavy to control the rotation.
prog: Add load or extend the eccentric to four seconds.
use: Efficient two-for-one when time is short. Hits biceps concentrically and forearm extensors eccentrically.

tech: Chest supported on an inclined surface with the arms hanging vertically, curl up with the upper arms perfectly still.
mist: Letting the chest come off the support. Swinging at the bottom.
prog: Add load or pause at peak contraction.
use: Peak-contraction emphasis. Good complement to incline curls, which cover the stretch.
mob: Biceps and forearm stretch against a wall

tech: Drag the dumbbells straight up the front of the torso by driving the elbows back, keeping the weights close to the body.
mist: Letting the elbows travel forward. Loading heavy enough that it becomes a standard curl.
prog: Add load or slow the eccentric.
use: Reduces front delt involvement, which makes the biceps do more of the work at the same load.
mob: Biceps and forearm stretch against a wall

tech: Stand on the band, curl with the elbows fixed, resist the return.
mist: Letting the band snap the arms down. Using tension so low that nothing accumulates.
prog: Shorten the band or double it.
use: Travel and finisher option. Tension peaks at the top where the biceps are already strong, so it is inferior to dumbbells for growth.
mob: Biceps and forearm stretch against a wall

tech: Hold at 90 degrees of elbow flexion with the elbows pinned, resist any drop.
mist: Letting the angle open gradually. Holding so long the position collapses.
prog: Add load or add time.
use: Finisher after curls, or a low-equipment option. Not a substitute for full-range work.
mob: Biceps and forearm stretch against a wall

tech: Torso as upright as balance allows, elbows tucked close to the ribs, descend to about 90 degrees of elbow flexion, press to full lockout.
mist: Leaning forward, which shifts the load to the chest. Bottoming out into an uncomfortable shoulder position.
prog: Add vest load or pause at the bottom.
use: The best triceps mass builder available without a barbell. Treat it as a main lift.
mob: Overhead triceps stretch, Anterior shoulder stretch

tech: Hands under the chest at roughly shoulder width or slightly narrower, elbows dragging close to the ribs, full lockout.
mist: Letting the elbows flare. Placing the hands so close the wrists complain.
prog: Elevate the feet or add a vest.
use: High-value triceps volume with zero setup. Good superset partner with curls.
mob: Overhead triceps stretch, Wrist mobility flow

tech: Index fingers and thumbs touching under the sternum, elbows tight, chest to hands.
mist: Wrist pain from an extreme hand position. Flaring the elbows to complete reps.
prog: Elevate the feet or add a vest.
use: Slightly more triceps than close-grip, at the cost of wrist comfort. Interchangeable.
mob: Wrist mobility flow, Overhead triceps stretch

tech: One dumbbell held with both hands overhead, elbows pointed forward and fixed, lower behind the head to a deep stretch, extend without locking hard.
mist: Letting the elbows flare wide. Cutting the stretch short, which is the productive part.
prog: Add load or pause two seconds in the stretch.
reg: Reduce load or perform one arm at a time.
use: The long head only gets fully lengthened when the shoulder is flexed, which pressing never achieves. This is essential, not optional.
mob: Overhead triceps stretch, Lat stretch on a doorframe

tech: One dumbbell overhead in one hand, opposite hand can brace the working elbow, lower deep behind the head.
mist: Leaning sideways to help. Letting the elbow drift outward.
prog: Add load or slow the eccentric.
use: Better for correcting arm asymmetry than the two-handed version.

tech: Lying on the floor or a surface, upper arms angled slightly back toward the head, lower the dumbbells beside the ears, extend.
mist: Letting the upper arms drift vertical, which removes tension at lockout. Flaring the elbows.
prog: Add load or add a pause at the bottom.
use: Reliable triceps mass movement. Angle the arms back to keep tension at the top.

tech: Hinged over, upper arm parallel to the torso and fixed, extend the elbow fully and hold for a beat.
mist: Swinging the upper arm. Loading heavy, which makes the movement pointless.
prog: Add a one-second squeeze rather than load.
use: Low priority. Tension is highest where the triceps is shortest, which is the least productive position. Pump work only.

tech: Hands on a stable edge behind you, legs out front, lower until the upper arm is roughly parallel to the floor, no deeper.
mist: Descending into an aggressive shoulder-extended position. Letting the hips drift away from the surface.
prog: Elevate the feet or place a weight plate or vest on the lap.
reg: Bend the knees and keep the feet close.
use: Fine accessory, but parallel bar dips are better in almost every way. Use when the dip station is unavailable.
mob: Anterior shoulder stretch, Overhead triceps stretch

tech: Hold an L-sit on parallettes and press up and down through a small range while the legs stay level.
mist: Legs dropping during the press. Attempting before a 20 second L-sit exists.
prog: Increase the range or raise the leg height.
use: Skill and triceps in one. Low volume, high demand.
mob: Wrist mobility flow, Hamstring floor stretch

tech: Band anchored overhead, elbows pinned at the sides, extend fully and control the return.
mist: Letting the elbows travel forward. Leaning over the band to add bodyweight.
prog: Shorten the band or add a squeeze at lockout.
use: Great warm-up and finisher. Tension profile favours the top, so pair it with overhead extensions.

tech: Dumbbells touching or nearly touching over the chest, elbows tucked tight, press with the triceps leading.
mist: Letting the elbows flare into a standard press. Bouncing off the floor.
prog: Add load or pause on the floor.
use: Heaviest triceps-biased press available with dumbbells. Good primary triceps movement on push days.

tech: Standing lean into the rings, arms overhead, allow the elbows to flex until the head passes the hands, extend back to a straight line.
mist: Piking at the hips to reduce load. Letting the elbows flare.
prog: Walk the feet forward to increase the lean.
use: Bodyweight long-head loading with a big stretch. Requires a hang point.
mob: Overhead triceps stretch, Wrist mobility flow

tech: Support hold at the top of a dip with the elbows locked, shoulders depressed, ribs down.
mist: Letting the shoulders shrug toward the ears. Holding with a soft, unlocked elbow.
prog: Add a vest or move to an L-sit support hold.
use: Builds the straight-arm support strength that dips, planche and muscle-ups all require.
mob: Anterior shoulder stretch, Wrist mobility flow

tech: Forearms resting on the thighs or a surface, palms up, let the dumbbell roll to the fingertips, then curl the wrist fully closed.
mist: Using a short range that skips the finger roll. Loading heavy enough to recruit the elbow.
prog: Add load or slow the eccentric.
use: Forearm mass and grip endurance. Two to four sets weekly is plenty.

tech: Palms down over the edge of a surface, raise the knuckles as high as possible, lower slowly.
mist: Using far too much weight. Lifting the forearm off the support.
prog: Add load or add a top hold.
use: Extensor work balances all the gripping you do and helps prevent elbow irritation from heavy pulling.

tech: Pronated grip, elbows pinned, curl to shoulder height, lower under control.
mist: Swinging because the load is too heavy for a pronated grip. Letting the wrists collapse into extension.
prog: Add load or slow the eccentric.
use: Best single forearm mass movement, and it visually thickens the top of the forearm near the elbow.
mob: Wrist mobility flow, Biceps and forearm stretch against a wall

tech: Heaviest dumbbells you can hold, ribs down, shoulders back, walk with controlled steps and normal breathing.
mist: Shrugging up into the ears. Leaning to one side under uneven load.
prog: Add load, add distance, or move to a single-arm suitcase carry.
use: Grip, traps, core and conditioning at once. One of the highest return per minute movements you own.

tech: One dumbbell at one side, resist the lateral lean, keep the shoulders level and walk tall.
mist: Letting the torso lean toward the weight. Rotating the shoulders.
prog: Add load or distance.
use: Anti-lateral-flexion core work plus grip. Also directly addresses left-right asymmetry.

tech: Full hang, active or passive, accumulate total time. Add vest load once a minute is easy.
mist: Chalking up nothing and quitting at the first burn instead of accumulating time. Holding the breath.
prog: Add vest load or move to one-arm hangs.
reg: Support some weight with the feet.
use: Grip strength has direct carryover to every pull you do, and hangs decompress the spine.

tech: Loop two towels over the bar and hang from the towel ends. Thick, uneven grip makes this far harder than a bar hang.
mist: Wrapping the towel around the hand so the grip is not actually working. Progressing before bar hangs are comfortable for a minute.
prog: Add time, then add vest load, then move to towel pull-ups.
reg: Use a single towel and support some weight on the feet.
use: Best crushing grip builder you own and it costs nothing.

tech: Pinch a dumbbell by the head or two plates smooth side out, hold at the side without letting the fingers slide.
mist: Cupping the fingers under the load. Holding until the object drops rather than stopping with control.
prog: Add load or time.
use: Pinch grip is the most neglected grip type and it transfers to everything you carry at work.

tech: A dowel or bar with a cord and a light weight. Roll up with the arms extended in front, then roll down under control.
mist: Using a load so heavy that the arms drop. Rushing the downward roll.
prog: Add load or roll with the arms fully extended at shoulder height.
reg: Reduce load or shorten the cord.
use: Extreme forearm pump and endurance. Optional, but effective if you build one.

tech: Push-up position supported on the fingertips with the fingers spread and slightly bent. Start against a wall or elevated.
mist: Starting on the floor before the fingers are conditioned. Letting a finger collapse into a locked hyperextension.
prog: Lower the surface height, then work toward the floor.
use: Advanced and slow to develop. Only worth it if the CRMO is quiet and the fingers feel healthy.

tech: Knees down, posterior pelvic tilt held throughout, roll out only as far as you can keep the lower back from arching, pull back by driving the ribs toward the pelvis rather than the hips backward.
mist: Letting the lower back sag at end range. Rolling back by hinging at the hips. Chasing range before control.
prog: Increase the rollout distance, then add a vest, then move toward standing.
reg: Reduce the distance or roll toward a wall stop.
use: The best loadable anterior core movement you own. This is the movement that actually builds abdominal thickness.

tech: From standing, roll out to full extension and return without the knees touching. Build with partial range against a wall first.
mist: Attempting before 15 clean kneeling reps at full range. Collapsing into lumbar extension at the bottom.
prog: Increase range toward a full body-length rollout.
reg: Return to kneeling rollouts or use a wall stop.
use: A genuine advanced core benchmark. Very few people can do it well.

tech: Hang, depress the shoulders, raise the legs to horizontal or higher by curling the pelvis under, lower with control and no swing.
mist: Swinging into the next rep. Raising the legs with pure hip flexion and no pelvic curl. Dropping the legs fast.
prog: Raise the legs higher toward the bar, add ankle load, or slow the lowering to four seconds.
reg: Use bent knees or the captain chair leg raise station.
use: Highest-value hanging core movement. The pelvic curl at the top is what makes it an ab exercise rather than a hip flexor exercise.
mob: Hamstring floor stretch, Dead hang decompression

tech: Knees to chest with a deliberate pelvic curl at the top, controlled descent.
mist: Using momentum from a swing. Stopping at 90 degrees of hip flexion without curling.
prog: Straighten the legs toward a full leg raise or add ankle load.
reg: Use the leg raise station with back support.
use: Main progression step toward hanging leg raises and toe-to-bar.

tech: Forearms on the pads, back against the support, raise the legs while curling the pelvis, avoid pushing through the shoulders.
mist: Letting the lower back arch off the pad. Swinging the legs.
prog: Straighten the legs, add ankle load, or move to hanging versions.
use: Back support removes the swing, so this is often better technique work than hanging versions early on.

tech: From a hang, compress the legs all the way to the bar with straight legs and no swing.
mist: Kipping the legs up. Bending the knees to reach.
prog: Slow the descent or add ankle load.
use: Strict version is a serious compression benchmark and it carries directly into front lever work.

tech: Hang with the legs raised, rotate them side to side under control, keeping the shoulders square to the bar.
mist: Letting the legs drop through the arc. Using momentum to swing from side to side.
prog: Straighten the legs fully or slow the tempo.
use: Advanced rotational and oblique work. Requires solid leg raises first.

tech: Lower back pressed flat into the floor, ribs down, arms and legs extended and held just off the ground.
mist: Any daylight under the lower back. Holding the breath.
prog: Extend the arms overhead, add time, or hold a light dumbbell.
reg: Tuck the knees or keep the arms at the sides.
use: The foundational position for every calisthenics skill you want. Non-negotiable for planche.

tech: Hold the hollow position and rock from the upper back to the hips without changing the body shape.
mist: Breaking the hollow shape to generate the rock. Rocking from the neck.
prog: Add time or hold a light weight overhead.
use: Teaches the body to keep tension while moving, which is the real skill.

tech: Face down, arms overhead, lift the chest, arms and legs, reaching long. The mirror image of a hollow hold.
mist: Cranking the neck. Lifting high instead of reaching long.
prog: Add time or hold light dumbbells.
use: Balances all the anterior core work and supports the posterior chain position for skills.

tech: Support on parallettes or dip bars, shoulders depressed, legs straight and level or above, quads locked, toes pointed.
mist: Shrugging into the shoulders. Letting the legs sag below parallel.
prog: Raise the legs above parallel toward a V-sit, or add ankle load.
reg: Use a tuck L-sit or one leg extended.
use: Hard compression strength that also builds straight-arm support. Direct feeder for planche.
mob: Hamstring floor stretch, Wrist mobility flow

tech: Support position with the knees tucked to the chest and feet off the floor, shoulders pushed down away from the ears.
mist: Letting the shoulders shrug. Resting the feet on the floor between reps.
prog: Extend one leg, then both.
reg: Support on a raised surface so the legs have more room.
use: Entry point for all compression work.

tech: Forearms under the shoulders, posterior pelvic tilt, glutes and quads engaged, squeeze hard rather than simply waiting out the clock.
mist: Sagging hips. Holding for minutes at low tension, which builds tolerance rather than strength.
prog: Add a vest, elevate the feet, or move to long-lever or RKC style tension.
reg: Perform from the knees or with hands elevated.
use: Best used as a short, maximally braced hold. Beyond 60 seconds it stops being productive.

tech: Plank with the elbows moved forward past the shoulders, which sharply increases the anti-extension demand.
mist: Letting the hips rise to reduce the lever. Holding past the point where the lower back gives up.
prog: Move the elbows further forward or add a vest.
use: Far harder than a standard plank at the same duration. Better use of time.

tech: Elbow under the shoulder, body in a straight line, hips stacked and lifted, top hand on the hip or reaching up.
mist: Hips sinking toward the floor. Rotating the chest toward the ground.
prog: Add a vest, raise the top leg, or add a hip dip.
use: Lateral core stability that most programs skip. Also useful for the left-right differences in your scan.

tech: From a side plank, lower the hip toward the floor under control and drive it back up to a straight line.
mist: Rotating the torso during the dip. Rushing the range.
prog: Add a vest or hold a dumbbell on the top hip.
use: Dynamic oblique loading. Obliques respond to load like any other muscle, and they frame the waist.

tech: One dumbbell in one hand, bend directly sideways through a full range, return to upright and slightly past.
mist: Twisting during the bend. Holding a dumbbell in each hand, which cancels the load.
prog: Add load or slow the eccentric.
use: Contested for waist aesthetics. Loading obliques adds thickness at the sides. If you want the narrowest possible waist, keep the load moderate and the reps higher.

tech: Band anchored at chest height to the side, press the hands straight out and resist the rotation, return slowly.
mist: Letting the torso rotate toward the anchor. Standing so close there is no tension.
prog: Step further from the anchor, shorten the band, or add a hold at full extension.
use: The cleanest anti-rotation movement available. Directly relevant to spinal control under asymmetric load at work.

tech: Hold the Pallof press at full extension and simply resist rotation for time.
mist: Bracing with the arms instead of the trunk. Allowing a slow rotational drift.
prog: Increase tension or add time.
use: Isometric version. Useful as a warm-up or a low-fatigue option.

tech: On the floor, curl the pelvis toward the ribs and lift the hips off the ground, lower slowly without letting the feet touch.
mist: Throwing the legs to generate momentum. Only flexing the hips without lifting the pelvis.
prog: Slow the eccentric, add ankle load, or elevate the hips on an incline.
reg: Keep the feet lighter and reduce range.
use: Rectus abdominis is one muscle, but this position biases the lower fibres through pelvic motion. Good pairing with rollouts.

tech: Hold a dumbbell at the chest or overhead, curl the ribs toward the pelvis through a short deliberate range, squeeze at the top.
mist: Pulling on the neck. Turning it into a sit-up driven by the hip flexors.
prog: Add load or pause at the top.
use: Abs are muscle. If you want thickness in the rectus, load it in the eight to fifteen rep range like any other muscle.

tech: Anchor the feet on a decline, curl the spine up segment by segment rather than hinging at the hips, hold a dumbbell for load.
mist: Yanking up with straight-line hip flexion. Jerking the neck forward.
prog: Add load or increase the decline.
reg: Reduce the decline or the load.
use: Loaded flexion through a long range. Hip flexors take some of the work, which is fine.

tech: Anchor the hands behind the head, lift the whole body onto the upper back and shoulders, lower as one rigid unit without letting the hips break.
mist: Piking at the hips on the descent. Attempting the full version before tuck and single-leg variants are solid.
prog: Progress from tuck to single-leg to straddle to full.
reg: Use a tuck position or negatives only.
use: One of the hardest anterior core movements that exists. Excellent, but earn it.

tech: Kneel facing a wall, roll out until the wheel touches the wall, return. Move further from the wall as control improves.
mist: Moving back before full range at the current distance is controlled. Losing the pelvic tilt at the wall.
prog: Move an inch or two further from the wall each week.
use: The safest way to build to full-range rollouts without the lower back paying for it.

tech: Lower back flat, extend the opposite arm and leg slowly while keeping the ribs down and the spine still.
mist: Letting the lower back lift off the floor. Moving fast enough that nothing is being controlled.
prog: Hold light dumbbells or slow the tempo.
reg: Move one limb at a time.
use: Low intensity, high value for learning bracing. Ideal warm-up or red-light day work.

tech: On hands and knees, extend the opposite arm and leg to a straight line without letting the hips rotate or the back arch.
mist: Lifting the leg above hip height and arching. Rotating the pelvis.
prog: Add a hold at end range or a light ankle weight.
reg: Move one limb at a time.
use: Spinal stability and glute activation. Good warm-up for lower days.

tech: Hang or use the leg raise station, raise the knees toward one shoulder with a deliberate pelvic rotation, alternate sides.
mist: Swinging into the rotation. Rotating from the shoulders instead of the trunk.
prog: Straighten the legs or add ankle load.
use: Direct oblique loading in a hanging position. Pairs well with straight leg raises.

tech: Side plank with the top leg supported on a surface at knee or ankle height, hips lifted, adductor of the top leg holding the position.
mist: Starting with the ankle on the support before the knee version is comfortable. Letting the hips drop.
prog: Move the support from the knee to the ankle, then add time.
reg: Support the bottom leg on the floor.
use: Adductor strength is a common weak link for hip health and single-leg work. Rare and worth including.

tech: Band anchored high, hold the handles beside the head, crunch the ribs down toward the pelvis with the hips still.
mist: Hinging at the hips instead of flexing the spine. Pulling with the arms.
prog: Shorten the band or add a pause at the bottom.
use: The closest thing to a cable crunch you can do at home. Loadable spinal flexion.

tech: Hollow body hold with the vest on the trunk. Position stays identical, load increases.
mist: Letting the lower back lift because of the added load. Adding the vest before a 45 second bodyweight hold exists.
prog: Add vest weight or add time.
use: Straightforward way to progressively overload an isometric that otherwise stalls.

tech: Forearm plank with the feet in rings or on sliders, shift the body forward and back while holding the plank shape.
mist: Letting the hips pike as the body slides back. Going further than the core can control.
prog: Increase the range of the saw or add a vest.
use: Dynamic anti-extension. Good substitute if the ab wheel irritates the wrists.

tech: Upper back on a stable surface, dumbbell across the hips on a pad, shins vertical at the top, chin tucked, drive to full hip extension and hold one second.
mist: Extending through the lumbar spine instead of the hip. Feet too close, which turns it into a quad movement.
prog: Add load, add a pause, or move to single-leg.
reg: Perform from the floor as a glute bridge.
use: Best direct glute loading available without a barbell, though dumbbell load caps out fairly quickly.

tech: From the floor, drive the hips up, squeeze hard at the top, hold one second.
mist: Using the hamstrings by placing the feet too far away. No pause at the top.
prog: Add load, elevate the shoulders, or move to single-leg.
use: Warm-up staple and a low-fatigue glute option.

tech: One foot planted, the other knee pulled toward the chest, drive the hip up while keeping the pelvis level.
mist: Letting the free-side hip drop. Arching the lower back.
prog: Add a dumbbell on the hip or elevate the shoulders.
use: Exposes side-to-side differences that bilateral work hides.

tech: Soles of the feet together, knees out, dumbbell on the hips, bridge up through a short range with continuous tension.
mist: Resting at the bottom between reps. Using a range so short nothing happens.
prog: Add load or add reps.
use: Pure pump work. Cheap and effective as a finisher.

tech: Band above the knees, seated or standing, push the knees apart against the band and pause at end range.
mist: Rocking the torso to help. Snapping back from end range.
prog: Shorten the band or add holds.
use: Glute medius work supports hip stability during heavy single-leg training and improves how the hip reads visually.

tech: Band above the knees, quarter squat position, step sideways with controlled tension and no heel drag.
mist: Letting the knees cave. Bouncing side to side.
prog: Use a thicker band or a lower stance.
use: Warm-up for lower days and a real fix for knee valgus during single-leg work.

tech: Front foot on a low platform, step back and lower the rear knee below the level of the front foot for extra range.
mist: Losing balance because the platform is too high. Torso collapsing forward.
prog: Add load or increase the deficit.
use: The extra range increases the glute stretch, which is where the growth stimulus is largest.
mob: Hip flexor lunge stretch, Pigeon stretch

tech: Band around the ankle anchored ahead, drive the leg back to full hip extension with the pelvis still, squeeze one second.
mist: Arching the lower back to gain range. Rotating the pelvis.
prog: Increase band tension or hold at end range.
use: Isolated hip extension. Accessory only, since compounds do the heavy lifting.

tech: Step up and drive the opposite knee to hip height at the top, controlled descent.
mist: Using the knee drive as momentum. Bounding rather than controlling.
prog: Add load or raise the box.
use: Athletic carryover and single-leg strength. Good finisher on a lower day.

tech: Move the front foot further forward and lean the torso forward roughly 30 degrees, which increases hip flexion at the bottom.
mist: Keeping the torso vertical, which makes it quad dominant. Rounding the back to lean.
prog: Add load or increase the forward lean.
use: Same movement, different emphasis. Rotate with the quad-biased version across training blocks.
mob: Pigeon stretch, Hip flexor lunge stretch

tech: Vest on, climb stairs or a steep incline taking full steps and driving through the whole foot.
mist: Running rather than driving each step. Excessive volume that interferes with lower day recovery.
prog: Add vest weight, duration, or step height.
use: Zone two cardio and glute work at once. Given your schedule, combining them is efficient.
mob: Calf stretch, Hip flexor lunge stretch

tech: Step the rear leg diagonally behind and across, lower under control, drive back to standing.
mist: Twisting the front knee inward. Going deeper than the hip range allows.
prog: Add load or increase depth.
use: Frontal plane glute work that straight-ahead lunges miss.

tech: Rear foot on a surface roughly knee height, front foot far enough forward that the shin stays near vertical at the bottom, descend until the rear knee is just off the floor, drive through the whole front foot.
mist: Front foot too close, which turns it into a knee-dominant lunge with no depth. Letting the torso collapse forward under load. Pushing off the back foot.
prog: Add dumbbell load, add a deficit under the front foot, or slow the eccentric.
reg: Hold a support with one hand or reduce depth.
use: The single best leg builder available without a barbell. This is your squat substitute. Legs are a named lagging area, so this earns a primary slot twice a week.
mob: Hip flexor lunge stretch, Quad stretch

tech: One dumbbell held at the chest, feet just outside shoulder width, sit down between the hips to full depth, chest tall, drive up without the hips shooting first.
mist: Depth cut short because the load is front-loaded. Heels lifting from limited ankle range.
prog: Add load, add a bottom pause, or elevate the heels.
reg: Reduce load or hold a support.
use: Best bilateral squat option you have, though your dumbbells cap the useful load fast. Once 55 pounds is easy for 15 reps, prioritise unilateral work instead.
mob: Ankle dorsiflexion drill, Deep squat hold

tech: Front foot on a low platform so the knee can travel further forward, torso upright, deep controlled descent.
mist: Letting the front heel lift. Bouncing at the bottom.
prog: Add load or increase the platform height.
use: More knee travel means more quad. Excellent when dumbbell load is the limiting factor.

tech: Step back, drop the rear knee toward the floor, keep the weight over the front foot, drive back to standing without pushing off the rear leg.
mist: Short steps that shift the load to the knee. Torso pitching forward.
prog: Add dumbbell or vest load, or add a deficit for the front foot.
reg: Reduce range or hold a support.
use: Easier on the knees than forward lunges and simpler to load than Bulgarians.

tech: Long strides, torso tall, controlled descent so the rear knee kisses the floor, drive up and through.
mist: Short strides that overload the knee. Rushing so the descent is uncontrolled.
prog: Add load or distance.
use: High systemic cost and excellent conditioning effect. Watch total fatigue given your work demands.
mob: Hip flexor lunge stretch, Quad stretch

tech: Box at or slightly above knee height, drive entirely through the top foot without pushing off the floor with the trailing leg, lower under control.
mist: Pushing off the bottom leg. Using a box so high the hip has to hitch.
prog: Add load or raise the box.
use: Very knee friendly and strongly unilateral. Good on days when the CRMO is grumbling.
mob: Quad stretch, Hip flexor lunge stretch

tech: Heels on a small wedge or plates, upright torso, deep squat with more knee travel and less hip contribution.
mist: Using an unstable elevation. Letting the knees cave inward.
prog: Add load or slow the eccentric.
use: Bias toward quads and a workaround for limited ankle dorsiflexion.

tech: Hold a support, rise onto the balls of the feet, drive the knees forward and lean the torso back in a straight line from knee to shoulder, descend under control.
mist: Progressing range too fast for the knees. Breaking at the hips.
prog: Reduce hand assistance, add a vest, or increase range.
reg: Use more hand support and less range.
use: Extreme quad stretch under load. Introduce gradually and stop at any sharp knee pain, especially with a CRMO history.
mob: Quad stretch, Hip flexor lunge stretch

tech: Build from box pistols, lowering the box height over time. Keep the heel down and the free leg straight ahead.
mist: Collapsing into the bottom rather than controlling it. Ignoring the ankle mobility requirement.
prog: Lower the box, then add a counterweight, then full pistols, then load a vest.
reg: Raise the box or hold a support.
use: Strength skill and a strong symmetry tool. Not the most efficient hypertrophy choice.
mob: Ankle dorsiflexion drill, Deep squat hold

tech: Back flat against the wall, thighs parallel, shins vertical, hold without shifting the weight to the heels.
mist: Sliding up as fatigue arrives. Holding the breath.
prog: Add a vest, hold a dumbbell, or move to single-leg.
use: Cheap quad finisher and useful when joints do not want dynamic load.

tech: Quarter to half squat, explode up, land softly by absorbing through the hips and knees.
mist: Chasing reps until the jumps get slow. Stiff landings.
prog: Add a light vest, but keep the reps low.
reg: Remove the jump and do fast bodyweight squats.
use: Power work. Given CRMO, keep the volume low and land quietly.

tech: Wide stance, shift the weight fully onto one bent leg while the other stays straight with the toes up, keep the heel down.
mist: Letting the heel lift. Rushing through the deepest range.
prog: Add a dumbbell held at the chest or increase depth.
reg: Hold a support or reduce depth.
use: Loaded adductor and hip range work. Rare quality that pays off in every other leg movement.

tech: Bodyweight squat mechanics with the vest on, full depth, controlled tempo.
mist: Treating it as cardio and losing depth. Letting the vest pull the torso forward.
prog: Add vest weight, slow the eccentric, or add a pause.
use: The vest alone rarely gives enough load for a strong lifter, so use it for higher reps or combine it with unilateral work.

tech: Soft knees held constant, push the hips back, keep the dumbbells close to the legs, lower until the hamstrings reach end range with a neutral spine, then drive the hips forward.
mist: Turning it into a squat by bending the knees. Rounding the lower back to reach further. Overextending at the top.
prog: Add load, slow the eccentric to four seconds, or elevate on a small platform for extra range.
use: Your primary hinge. Hamstrings are a named weak point and this is the most loadable option you own.

tech: Hinge over one leg with the free leg extending back in line with the torso, hips square, dumbbell tracking down the standing leg.
mist: Letting the hip of the free leg open toward the ceiling. Balancing rather than loading, so the hamstring never works hard.
prog: Add load or slow the eccentric.
reg: Touch the free foot lightly to the floor for balance.
use: Hamstring work plus balance plus asymmetry correction. Load lighter than you expect.

tech: Anchor the ankles under a heavy surface, keep the hips extended and the body in one line, lower as slowly as possible, catch with the hands and push back up.
mist: Breaking at the hips to reduce the lever. Free-falling instead of resisting.
prog: Increase the range you control before catching, or reduce band assistance.
reg: Use a band anchored overhead, or perform partials in the top range.
use: The strongest eccentric hamstring stimulus that exists, and the best hamstring injury protection. Two to four sets weekly is enough.
mob: Quad stretch, Standing hamstring hinge stretch

tech: One dumbbell held at the chest or on the upper back, hinge to roughly horizontal with a neutral spine, drive back up.
mist: Rounding the back under load. Bending the knees to reach lower.
prog: Add load or slow the eccentric.
use: Erector and hamstring work with a different loading profile from the RDL. Keep the load moderate.

tech: Lie on your back with the heels on sliders or a towel on a smooth floor, bridge the hips up, extend the legs out and curl them back while keeping the hips high.
mist: Letting the hips drop as the legs extend. Using a surface with too much friction.
prog: Move to single-leg or slow the extension.
reg: Reduce range or keep the hips lower.
use: The only knee flexion movement you own besides Nordics, and much easier to program for volume.

tech: Same as the two-leg version with one heel on the slider and the other leg held off the floor.
mist: Dropping the hips. Attempting before 15 clean two-leg reps.
prog: Slow the eccentric or add a pause at full extension.
use: Big step up in difficulty. Great asymmetry work.

tech: Upper back on a stable surface, one foot planted, drive the hip to full extension with a posterior pelvic tilt at the top, pause one second.
mist: Hyperextending the lower back instead of extending the hip. Pushing through the toes.
prog: Add a dumbbell across the hip or slow the eccentric.
use: Direct glute loading with minimal equipment. Glutes matter for how the whole lower body reads.

tech: Heels elevated on a surface, drive the hips up until the body is a straight line from knee to shoulder, squeeze for one second.
mist: Arching the lower back to gain height. Rushing the reps.
prog: Add a vest or a dumbbell across the hips, or move to single-leg.
reg: Keep the feet on the floor.
use: Heel elevation shifts more of the work to the hamstrings. Good accessory after RDLs.

tech: Wide stance, dumbbells between the feet, hinge with a vertical torso angle steeper than a conventional pull, drive the floor away.
mist: Squatting the weight up. Letting the dumbbells drift forward.
prog: Add load or stand on a small platform for extra range.
use: Adductor and glute emphasis. Useful variety, but the RDL remains the priority hinge.
mob: Adductor stretch, Standing hamstring hinge stretch

tech: Lie face down with the hips at the edge of a stable surface, legs hanging, raise them to hip height by squeezing the glutes, no lumbar cranking.
mist: Swinging the legs up with momentum. Hyperextending the lower back.
prog: Add ankle weight or a pause at the top.
use: Low-compression posterior chain work. Kind to the spine after a long day of physical work.

tech: Ball of the foot on an edge, drop into a deep stretch for a full second, then rise as high as possible and hold the top for a second.
mist: Bouncing out of the stretch, which uses the tendon rather than the muscle. Short range at both ends.
prog: Add dumbbell load or slow the eccentric to three seconds.
reg: Use both legs or reduce range.
use: Calves need range and pauses more than they need weight. The stretch position is doing most of the work.

tech: Seated with the knees bent to 90 degrees, dumbbells on the lower thighs, balls of the feet on a block, full stretch and full contraction with pauses.
mist: Letting the dumbbells slide toward the knee. Half reps.
prog: Add load or lengthen the pauses.
use: The bent knee position takes the gastrocnemius out and targets the soleus, which straight-leg raises largely miss.

tech: Vest on, both feet on an edge, full range with a one second stretch and a one second squeeze.
mist: Rushing to accumulate reps. Skipping the bottom stretch.
prog: Add vest weight or move to single leg.
use: Convenient way to load bilateral calf work without holding dumbbells.

tech: Hinged at the hips with the hands on a surface, balls of the feet on an edge, vest on the hips, full range.
mist: Bouncing. Bending the knees.
prog: Add vest weight or slow the eccentric.
use: The hip-flexed position lengthens the gastrocnemius slightly. Old-school and effective.

sec: Tibialis anterior, foot intrinsics, cardiovascular system
tech: Stay on the balls of the feet, small hops, relaxed shoulders, wrists doing the work.
mist: Landing heavy on the heels. Long sets that beat up the shins.
prog: Add time, single-leg hops, or double unders.
use: Conditioning plus calf endurance. Keep the impact volume moderate given CRMO.

tech: Three second pause in the fully stretched bottom position, then a controlled rise and a two second squeeze at the top.
mist: Shortening the pause when it burns. Reducing the range to keep the load.
prog: Add load or lengthen the pause.
use: If your calves have never grown, the reason is almost always missing range and missing pauses, not missing volume.

tech: Small fast hops on one leg with a stiff ankle and quiet landings.
mist: Landing loudly and collapsing at the ankle. High volume that irritates the shins.
prog: Add height or distance, not reps.
use: Ankle stiffness and reactive strength. Low volume, high quality.

tech: Heavy dumbbells, rise onto the balls of the feet and walk without the heels touching down.
mist: Letting the heels drop between steps. Loading so heavy that the grip fails first.
prog: Add load or time.
use: Calves, grip and core in one. Efficient finisher.

tech: Back against a wall, heels a foot or so out, raise the toes toward the shins through full range, lower slowly.
mist: Bouncing. Letting the heels roll.
prog: Step the feet further from the wall, add a vest, or move to single leg.
use: Tibialis strength supports ankle health, knee tracking and shin comfort during high step-count work days.

tech: Seated with a dumbbell hooked over the toes or a band around the forefoot, dorsiflex fully and lower under control.
mist: Using load that forces a short range. Letting the dumbbell slip.
prog: Add load or slow the eccentric.
use: Loadable tibialis work once wall raises become easy.

tech: Walk on the heels with the toes pulled up as high as possible.
mist: Letting the toes drop. Short choppy steps.
prog: Hold dumbbells or add time.
use: Simple and effective. Costs nothing and can be done between sets.

tech: Band anchored ahead and looped over the forefoot, pull the toes back toward the shin, control the return.
mist: Moving from the knee. Snapping back to the start.
prog: Increase tension or add holds.
use: Portable option. Useful in the truck or at work during breaks.

tech: Press the head into your own hand or a wall in flexion, extension and each side, building tension gradually and releasing gradually. No head movement.
mist: Ramping tension too fast. Holding the breath.
prog: Increase the duration or the intensity of the press.
use: Safest entry to neck training. A developed neck visibly changes how the jaw and shoulders frame, which is directly relevant to your goals.
mob: Upper trap and levator stretch, Chin tuck

tech: Lie on your back with the head off the edge of a surface, tuck the chin and curl the head up slowly, lower with equal control.
mist: Jutting the chin forward instead of tucking. Adding load before several weeks of bodyweight work.
prog: Add a light weight on a folded towel over the forehead after four to six weeks.
reg: Perform with the head on the surface.
use: Build slowly. Neck tissue adapts more slowly than limb musculature.
mob: Chin tuck, Upper trap and levator stretch

tech: Face down with the head off the edge, raise the head to neutral and slightly beyond through a controlled short range.
mist: Cranking into deep extension. Fast reps.
prog: Add a light towel-wrapped weight only after several weeks.
use: Extensors balance the flexion work and support head position during heavy carries and hanging.

tech: Lie on your side with the head off the edge, raise the head laterally through a short controlled range.
mist: Using momentum. Excessive range.
prog: Add a very light weight after several weeks.
use: Completes the neck in all planes. Low volume is sufficient.

tech: Draw the chin straight back to make a double chin without tilting the head down, hold, release.
mist: Tilting the head down instead of translating back. Forcing the range.
prog: Add time or perform against light hand resistance.
use: The direct counter to forward head posture, which is costing you visible height and jaw definition. Do this several times daily.
mob: Chin tuck, Upper trap and levator stretch

tech: Standing, move one arm through the largest circle you can control with no torso movement, breathing steadily. Slow means thirty seconds per circle, not five.
mist: Compensating with the ribs and spine. Rushing.
prog: Slow the circle down or increase the range at the sticking point.
use: Pre-workout for any pressing or pulling session. Also good on rest days.

tech: Back and arms against a wall, ribs down, slide the arms overhead keeping the wrists and elbows in contact as long as possible.
mist: Arching the lower back to gain range. Letting the elbows leave the wall immediately.
prog: Hold at end range for a breath, or add a light band around the wrists.
reg: Move the feet further from the wall.
use: Warm-up before overhead pressing and a daily posture drill.

n: Thoracic Extension over a Rolled Towel
tech: Rolled towel or foam roller across the mid back, hands supporting the head, extend over the roller and breathe out slowly. Move the roller one segment at a time.
mist: Extending through the lower back instead of the thoracic spine. Holding the breath.
prog: Add a light dumbbell held overhead.
use: Post-workout and daily. Direct counter to the rounded upper back that a phone and a work van produce.

tech: Forearm on a doorframe with the elbow at shoulder height, step through and rotate away, ribs down. Repeat with the elbow high and low for different fibres.
mist: Letting the ribs flare so the stretch moves to the shoulder capsule. Bouncing.
prog: Raise or lower the arm position, or increase the step through.
use: Post-push sessions and daily. Tight pecs pull the shoulders forward and cost you visible height.

tech: Place a ball just below the collarbone near the shoulder, lean into a wall and breathe slowly, adding small arm movements.
mist: Pressing directly on the shoulder joint. Rolling too fast to allow any change.
prog: Add arm movement during the hold.
use: Before pull sessions and after long days holding tools overhead.

tech: Hold a doorframe or bar at chest height, sit the hips back and away from the arm, let the ribs open on that side.
mist: Shrugging the shoulder up. Rushing into the end range.
prog: Rotate the torso slightly away for more range.
use: After every pull session. Tight lats limit overhead position and pull the ribs down.

tech: Full passive hang, feet off the floor, let the shoulders rise toward the ears and the spine lengthen. Breathe.
mist: Holding actively the entire time, which defeats the decompression. Dropping off the bar suddenly.
prog: Add time or add a slight side to side sway.
reg: Support some weight with the feet.
use: Daily. Gives a genuine quarter to half inch of temporary height and is one of the few honest levers you have there.

tech: Hands behind you on a chair or bench edge, walk the feet forward and sink the hips to open the front of the shoulder.
mist: Sinking too fast into an aggressive range. Shrugging.
prog: Walk the feet further forward.
use: After dips and pressing. Do not force this one if the shoulder is irritated.

n: Biceps and Forearm Stretch Against a Wall
tech: Palm flat on a wall behind you at shoulder height with the fingers pointing back, rotate the torso away.
mist: Forcing the elbow into hyperextension. Bouncing.
prog: Rotate further or raise the hand height.
use: After heavy pulling or curling. Also useful for elbow health with high pull-up volume.

tech: On hands and knees, rock forward and back with the fingers forward, then fingers back, then palms up, then on the knuckles, ten slow reps each.
mist: Loading straight into the deepest position cold. Skipping it before planche work.
prog: Increase the lean or add reps.
use: Mandatory before any planche, handstand or parallette session. Wrists are the usual injury site in calisthenics.

tech: Reach one hand down the spine, use the other to gently draw the elbow back and up, ribs down.
mist: Flaring the ribs to gain range. Cranking hard on the elbow.
prog: Add a slight side bend away.
use: After triceps and pressing work.

tech: Tilt the ear toward one shoulder for the upper trap, then rotate the nose toward the armpit for the levator, with the opposite hand anchoring the shoulder down.
mist: Pulling hard on the head. Letting the anchored shoulder rise.
prog: Anchor the down-side hand under a seat.
use: After shrugs, carries and long work days. Also helps with tension headaches.

tech: Draw the chin straight back without tilting, hold two seconds, release. Do it standing against a wall to check position.
mist: Nodding down instead of translating back. Forcing the range.
prog: Add hold time or light hand resistance.
