use: Several times a day, especially after phone use. Forward head posture is the single biggest silent cost to your standing height.

tech: On hands and knees, move slowly between full flexion and full extension one segment at a time, matching the breath.
mist: Moving only at the lower back. Rushing.
prog: Slow the tempo and increase segmental control.
use: Warm-up for anything, and a good reset after long driving or crouching at work.

tech: Side lying with the knees stacked and bent at 90 degrees, rotate the top arm open toward the floor behind you and follow it with the eyes.
mist: Letting the knees separate to gain fake range. Rushing the rotation.
prog: Hold the end range for a full exhale.
use: Before pressing and rowing, and after asymmetric work days.

tech: Standing or kneeling, reach one arm overhead and side bend away, breathing into the stretched ribs.
mist: Bending forward instead of laterally. Holding the breath.
prog: Add a slight rotation.
use: After oblique and carry work.

tech: Knees wide, hips back to the heels, arms reaching long, chest sinking toward the floor, slow breathing.
mist: Letting the shoulders shrug. Holding tension in the neck.
prog: Walk the hands to one side for a lat bias.
reg: Place a cushion under the hips.
use: Downregulation at the end of a session, especially useful on high stress days.

tech: Half kneeling, tuck the pelvis under and squeeze the rear glute before shifting forward. The tuck is what makes it work.
mist: Arching the lower back and feeling it in the spine. Shifting forward without the posterior tilt.
prog: Raise the same-side arm overhead and side bend away.
use: Daily. Tight hip flexors tilt the pelvis forward, which shortens your apparent height and pushes the belly out.

tech: Standing or half kneeling with the rear foot elevated against a wall, pelvis tucked under, torso tall.
mist: Arching the back to gain range. Letting the knee flare out.
prog: Elevate the rear foot higher.
reg: Use a standing version holding the ankle.
use: After leg days and heavy split squat work.

tech: One heel on a low surface with the toes up, hinge from the hips with a flat back until the hamstring loads.
mist: Rounding the spine to reach further. Locking the knee hard.
prog: Raise the surface or add a slight ankle dorsiflexion.
use: After hinge work. A flat-back hinge position is the point, not touching the toes.

tech: On your back, band or towel around one foot, raise the leg with the knee straight and the opposite leg flat on the floor.
mist: Letting the opposite leg lift. Pulling hard enough to round the pelvis off the floor.
prog: Add ankle dorsiflexion or raise the leg further.
use: Safest hamstring stretch and it supports the compression positions needed for L-sits and leg raises.

tech: Sit into the deepest squat you can hold with the heels down, elbows inside the knees pressing gently out, chest tall.
mist: Letting the heels lift. Collapsing into a fully rounded position without intent.
prog: Add gentle rocking or reach one arm overhead.
reg: Hold a doorframe or elevate the heels.
use: Daily. Restores the hip and ankle range that heavy work and driving strip away.

tech: Front shin angled across in front, rear leg extended straight back, hips square, fold forward over the front leg.
mist: Letting the hips rotate open. Forcing the front knee into an uncomfortable angle.
prog: Square the hips further or fold deeper.
reg: Perform the figure four version lying on your back.
use: After lower days and long periods of sitting or crouching.

tech: Wide kneeling straddle or a frog position, rock the hips back gently and hold at the point of tension, not pain.
mist: Forcing depth. Letting the lower back round hard.
prog: Widen the stance or rock further back.
use: Supports Cossack squats, deep squats and general hip health.

tech: Half kneeling facing a wall, drive the knee forward over the toes without lifting the heel, aiming to increase the distance from wall to toe over time.
mist: Letting the heel lift. Letting the arch collapse inward.
prog: Move the foot further from the wall or add a band pulling the ankle back.
use: Before squats and split squats. Ankle range is the most common limiter on squat depth.

tech: Straight rear leg against a wall for the gastrocnemius, then bend that knee for the soleus. Hold each.
mist: Only doing the straight leg version, which misses the soleus. Letting the foot roll outward.
prog: Elevate the toes on a step.
use: After calf work and after long days on your feet.
